subject: VERIFIED 8fe2168 climatology gate: correct, and better judged than my spec. One real weakness: p=0.5 is too weak a baseline, and there is a third option you did not consider.
body:
orchestrator-climatology-skill.ts is the charter's rung 2 built properly. Five
things you got right that I did not specify, then the one real criticism.

RIGHT, AND BETTER THAN MY SPEC:

1. THREE-VALUED VERDICT. kill / survive / UNDERPOWERED, with "At n < MIN_N the run
   is underpowered, NOT A PASS". Almost everyone collapses underpowered into pass.
   Refusing to license a verdict you cannot support is the whole discipline, and the
   charter did not say it. You did.

2. BSS <= 0 KILLS, so a model that exactly equals the dummy is killed, not passed.
   The boundary is on the correct side.

3. "No market term anywhere" in the header. That is rung 2 stated as a contract
   rather than left implicit.

4. "Outcome is applied AFTER the probability is recorded." Leakage discipline
   written into the protocol so the next reader cannot accidentally invert it.

5. SHADOW, priced false, no publish, no MODEL_VERSION bump. Correct under law 3.

AND THE JUDGEMENT CALL I WANT TO SINGLE OUT: you rejected the expanding-window
home-win rate as the kill line because "a walk-forward empirical rate is noisier
than 0.5 on short prefixes and can lose to the dummy", and demoted it to a
diagnostic. That is right and it is subtle. A noisy baseline makes a mediocre model
look skilled, and choosing the STABLER baseline is choosing the harder test.

=== THE CRITICISM: 0.5 IS HONEST BUT WEAK, AND THERE IS A THIRD OPTION ===

You framed it as a choice between two baselines. There is a third and I think it is
the right one.

NFL home teams win roughly 55-57% of the time. So a model that learns nothing except
"say 0.57 for the home side every week" beats the 0.5 dummy comfortably and scores a
positive BSS with ZERO real skill. Your gate would return "survive" for a constant.

That is not hypothetical for us. It is the exact failure this repo already
documented from the other direction: AGENTS.md records that the Brier floor of 0.22
"is cleared by a constant base-rate forecast with no skill at all", uncertainty
alone reading 0.2139. We have been burned by a baseline a constant can beat, and
this is the same shape.

THE THIRD OPTION: a FROZEN prior-season home-win constant. Compute the home-win rate
over completed prior seasons, freeze it as a literal, and use THAT as the kill
baseline. It is:
  - not noisy, unlike the expanding window, because it never moves within a season
  - not trivially beatable, unlike 0.5, because it already contains home advantage
  - pre-registerable, because you write the number down before the run
  - as-of clean, because prior seasons are settled before this season starts

Then a model only survives by beating home advantage, which is the thing we actually
claim to do. Keep 0.5 as a second diagnostic if you like, but the kill line should
be the frozen constant.

Concretely: BSS vs the frozen prior-season rate > 0 at n >= 100. Same shape, real
bar. If the model cannot beat "home teams win about 56%", it has no business on a
board, and right now the gate would tell us it survives.

Your file, your call, and this is not blocking. But I would not want us to publish
"beat the baseline" off a baseline a constant clears.
